cases.name: late receipt: the EP23755468 letter received 11 days after its date gives a note of 4 days and no change of the due date
derivation: R.126(2) and R.127(2) EPC: the document is deemed delivered on the date it bears, 2026-06-09. R.131(2) EPC: computation starts on 2026-06-10.
R.131(4) EPC: 4 months after 9 June 2026 is 9 October 2026, an open Friday.

R.126(2) and R.127(2) EPC: only if the EPO establishes receipt more than seven days after the date, the period ends later by the days beyond seven: 11 - 7 = 4 days, 9 October + 4 days = 13 October 2026.
The library cannot prove that fact, so the due date stays 9 October 2026 and the later date is a note, as in ep.r71-3.grant-communication v1.

cases.name: refusal: no period in the input
derivation: R.71(1) EPC: the period is "a period to be specified" in the communication. The law gives no default, so the engine computes no date.

cases.name: refusal: a period of null
derivation: A JavaScript or JSON caller can send null. It is the same as no period.

cases.name: refusal: a period of one month
derivation: R.132(2) EPC: a period that the EPO specifies is not less than two months. R.71(1) EPC provides nothing else.

cases.name: refusal: a period of zero months
derivation: R.132(2) EPC: not less than two months.

cases.name: refusal: a period of seven months
derivation: R.132(2) EPC: not more than four months, in certain circumstances up to six months. Seven months is outside the range.

cases.name: refusal: a period that is not a whole number of months
derivation: R.131(1) EPC lays down periods in full years, months, weeks or days. 4.5 months is not a period in full months.

cases.name: refusal: a period given as text
derivation: The input must be a number of months. The text "4" is not parsed.

cases.name: refusal: document date before effectiveFrom
derivation: The rule applies from 2023-11-01, when the new R.126(2) and R.127(2) EPC apply (CA/D 10/22, OJ EPO 2022, A101). A document of 31 October 2023 is under the old ten-day rule.

cases.name: refusal: the first document date of the rule version needs the 2024 calendar, which is not loaded
derivation: R.131(4) EPC: 2 months after 1 November 2023 is 1 January 2024. R.134(1) EPC needs the 2024 calendar, which the library does not load.

cases.name: refusal: due date in 2028, a year with no calendar
derivation: R.131(4) EPC: 4 months after 15 September 2027 is 15 January 2028. R.134(1) EPC needs the 2028 calendar, which the library does not load.

cases.name: refusal: the closure from 24 December 2027 continues into 2028, a year with no calendar
derivation: R.131(4) EPC: 4 months after 24 August 2027 is 24 December 2027, closed (OJ EPO 2026, A30). The closure runs to 31 December 2027, and 1 January 2028 needs the 2028 calendar.

cases.name: refusal: event EPO:R71(3) does not trigger the rule
derivation: The rule triggers only on EPO:A94(3).
